one_liner: Magento/Adobe Commerce has broad REST and GraphQL web APIs; each merchant hosts its own instance, so base URL and credentials are per-customer (integration OAuth 1.0a, or admin/customer bearer tokens).
auth_notes: Pages show Magento Open Source/PaaS integrations use OAuth 1.0a with HMAC-SHA256 signed requests (OTHER, not OAuth2). Admin and customer tokens are exchanged for username/password and sent as Bearer tokens; integration access token can be used as a standalone bearer token if enabled (API_KEY-like). IMS access tokens are mentioned for Commerce Admin IMS integration; Cloud Service auth details are not in the pages, so OAUTH2 is not claimed.
access_notes: Pages do not state pricing. Merchants create integrations in their own Admin, which generates credentials; a developer running an Open Source install can do so, but this is not directly confirmed on the pages. Low confidence.
blocker_notes: Every merchant runs its own instance, so a toolkit needs a per-customer base URL and merchant-created integration credentials, with OAuth 1.0a request signing. The supplied pages show no MCP server, and the draft's community MCP URL is not supported by them, so it was removed.

evidence.quote: The Commerce Web APIs allow you to integrate third-party software and build headless applications for Adobe Commerce. The Web API documentation is divided into three guides: REST, GraphQL, and Getting Started.
OAuth authentication with Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source is based on [OAuth 1.0a](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5849), an open standard for secure API authentication.
When you request a token from one of these services, the service returns a unique access token in exchange for an account's username and password.
For most web API calls, you supply this token in the `Authorization` request header with the `Bearer` HTTP authorization scheme to prove your identity.
The merchant creates an integration from Admin. Commerce generates a consumer key and a consumer secret.
